programme: No single module. The concordant factors span at least four unrelated programmes with no shared targets or complex membership: PPARG-driven adipocyte/lipid and anti-inflammatory signaling (SREBF1/2, FABP4, CD36, LPL, TNF, PTGS2 among its targets); ETS2-linked proliferation/apoptosis control (TP53, CDKN1A/CDKN2A, MDM2, BCL2L1); TFDP2/E2F-type cell-cycle entry (MYC, PCNA, RFC3); HOXB2 and HOXA11 developmental/ECM patterning (KRT8/14, MMP9, COL3A1); CD40-axis costimulation via AKNA (CD40, CD40LG) and T-cell regulation via BCL11B; and MUC1, an epithelial mucin, sitting apart from all of these. HR is ambiguous terminology (hormone-receptor status, not a distinct regulator) and TCF15/ST18 have no mechanistic support at all. These do not cohere into one recognizable complex or pathway the way a named module (e.g. ISGF3) would.
role_in_a: Individually, several factors have documented breast-cancer roles (PPARG in tumor lipid metabolism/PPAR-agonist studies, ETS2 in ferroptosis/proliferation control, TFDP2 in triple-negative breast cancer, HOXB2 in ECM remodeling, MUC1 as a classical breast tumor antigen/marker) — but these are independent, disease-generic cancer-biology findings, not steps of one shared programme.
role_in_b: For IBS specifically there is essentially no mechanistic literature for any of these factors. PPARG and MUC1 carry Open Targets associations with IBS, but the retrieved MUC1 papers concern IBD and peptic ulcer disease, not IBS itself, which is a distinct, non-inflammatory functional disorder.
shared_axis: No documented or mechanistically plausible shared axis emerges. The apparent recurrence of these factors across patient-group comparisons more likely reflects broadly expressed cancer/inflammation-adjacent genes being picked up independently in each disease's network than a common regulatory process linking breast cancer to IBS.
reasoning: The factors belong to at least four distinct, non-interacting regulatory programmes with no shared targets, complex membership, or annotated pathway; forcing a single 'module' story here would violate the instruction to keep incoherent available. The only factor with literature in both diseases (MUC1) is supported for IBS only by papers actually about IBD/peptic ulcer disease, not IBS, so even that link does not hold up.
support: PMID 41230773 — PPARG expression change in breast cancer, no IBS relevance. PMID 42602283 and 39796183 — ETS2 mechanistic role in breast carcinogenesis/ferroptosis, breast-only. PMID 39710273 — TFDP2 in triple-negative breast cancer, breast-only. PMID 38322121 — HOXB2 limits triple-negative breast carcinogenesis, breast-only. PMID 42054195, 42487010, 42068440, 41506350 — MUC1 as breast cancer marker/therapeutic target, breast-only. PMID 41350285 — intestinal Mucin-1 barrier study, concerns metabolic dysfunction, not IBS specifically. PMID 41284256 — mucin signatures reviewed for Inflammatory Bowel Disease, not IBS. PMID 33608531 — GWAS of peptic ulcer disease, not IBS.
how_to_falsify: Take matched breast tumor and IBS colonic mucosal biopsies from the same cohort and test whether PPARG and MUC1 (the only two factors with any cross-disease evidence) are co-expressed or co-regulated at the protein level; if their expression is uncorrelated and no shared upstream/downstream partners are found by co-IP or ChIP-seq, the claim of any shared axis is falsified. More broadly, a formal enrichment test showing the combined target sets of these 12 factors do not converge on any common annotated pathway (beyond chance) would confirm incoherence.
caveats: Breast and colorectal tissue are anatomically and physiologically distinct, and the 156 patient-group comparisons derive from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the large comparison count likely reflects repeated subgroup splits of a small number of underlying studies rather than independent replication. MECOM and HOXB2 are marked discordant, meaning their recurrence does not represent agreement between the two diseases and they were excluded from consideration here. The exclusion of single-view factors (PREB, NR1H4, TRIM22, TEAD2, CHD4, L3MBTL1, ZBTB10) removes subgroup-specific noise but does not change the underlying heterogeneity of the remaining list. IBS and IBD are distinct disease entities; most 'IBS-relevant' literature retrieved here is actually about IBD or peptic ulcer disease and should not be treated as IBS evidence.
